meta.title: e2ugh v6 - Unified Virtual Processor Database
meta.description: Union of the v5 canonical CPU database (6 x86_64 identities), the E2ugh processor catalog (55 SKUs incl. ARM/Apple/Xeon), Zen5/X3D microarchitecture specs and pool minis. Field conflicts resolved V5-first (model_name/max_boost_ghz/tdp_watts canonical); OMNI complementary fields (arch, core_type, topology, memory_support, release_date) merged in place. Versions re-pinned date-first 2026-08-22.

families.avx512Notes: Full 512-bit datapaths on Zen 5. Subsets: F, DQ, CD, BW, VL, IFMA, VBMI, VBMI2, VPOPCNTDQ, BITALG, VNNI, BF16; AVX512_FP16 is new in Zen 5. sha_ni present since Zen 1.

codenames: Turin Dense (EPYC 9005 dense CCDs, including 9965 and 9955)
families.avx512Notes: ISA identical to Zen 5 (compact core, not a cut-down ISA): full AVX-512 incl. FP16 and BF16, sha_ni.
families.notes: Same ISA and per-core caches as Zen 5; smaller die area, lower clocks, and 16 MB L3 per 8-core CCD (vs 32 MB on standard Zen 5 CCDs).

families.avx512Notes: AVX-512 with double-pumped 256-bit datapath (AVX-512 executes at half rate vs Zen 5). Subsets: F, DQ, CD, BW, VL, IFMA, VBMI, VBMI2, VPOPCNTDQ, BITALG, VNNI, BF16 plus VAES/GFNI/VPCLMULQDQ. No AVX512_FP16.

families.smtNote: Arrow Lake client silicon has no Hyper-Threading: 24 cores report exactly 24 logical CPUs.
families.avx512Notes: AVX-512 removed from Intel client silicon since Alder Lake; Arrow Lake reports AVX2 + AVX-VNNI (no avx512f family flags).
families.qemuModel: Skylake-Client-noTSX-IBRS or Cascadelake-Server (closest TCG models without AVX-512: prefer explicit -cpu with -avx512 flags removed)

notes: CPUID family for all Zen 5 / Zen 5c parts = 26 (0x1A); Zen 4 (Threadripper 7980X) = 25 (0x19); Intel Arrow Lake = family 6, model 0xC0.
Granite Ridge desktop (9950X3D) CPUID model is 0x44 (68 decimal) in family 26; for Turin dense server parts verify the model ID against a live hardware dump before production spoofing.

TCG emulates SSE through AVX/AVX2; AVX-512 guest instructions are not fully translated under TCG. For pure CPUID/proc spoofing use the LD_PRELOAD hook on the host instead of relying on guest execution.
lscpu reads sysfs + /proc/cpuinfo (man7 lscpu.1); free parses /proc/meminfo; both are covered by the LD_PRELOAD open/openat/fopen interception family.

epyc9965: Address sizes:           52 bits physical, 57 bits virtual

procCpuinfoSpoof.hookStrategy: LD_PRELOAD intercept of open/open64/openat/fopen/fopen64/freopen/freopen64 redirected to a regenerated /tmp/cpuinfo_scaled, plus sysinfo()/uname() hooks with dlsym(RTLD_NEXT); static/Go binaries require the seccomp SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF + SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ADDFD fallback tier.
